title: Applied ML Quality Guardrails and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Priya Natarajan
content:
SUMMARY
This playbook describes the end-to-end applied ML evaluation (eval) and regression triage practices used at Redwood Inference. It combines guidance and runnable procedures for:
- Eval harness onboarding and continuous integration
- Prompt set curation and benchmark definition
- Model onboarding acceptance criteria
- Production-quality guardrails (safety, factuality, cost, latency)
- Quantization profile recommendations and risk matrix
- Regression triage runbook for rapid root-cause and rollback

SCOPE
Covers any model or model-variant being considered for serving on Redwood API, Redwood Dedicated, or Redwood Private. Applies to research-model onboarding, open-model variants, and quantized artifacts used for production inference. Excludes experimental research-only prototypes not intended for deployment.

OWNERSHIP AND ROPES
- Document owner: Applied ML / Eval team (owner_team: engineering)
- Primary contacts: Priya Natarajan (applied-ml), Liam Chen (eval-harness infra)
- Oncall for regressions: eng-sre pager for infra, applied-ml escalation for eval quality

KEY METRICS AND SLOs (EVAL GUARDRAILS)
- Latency (99th): <= 200 ms for short text endpoints, <= 600 ms for long-sequence pathways (thresholds adjustable per route)
- Tokenized cost delta: new model token-cost must be <= +15% vs baseline unless quality gain justified in PRD
- Hallucination / factuality: oracle-verified hallucination rate <= 3% on curated factual prompt set (see Prompt Set Catalog)
- Semantic similarity: embedding-based mean cosine similarity to reference >= 0.78 on dev benchmark
- Toxicity: P(toxic) <= 0.5% on safety prompt set (use Perspective API / internal safety eval)
- Regression alert threshold: any single-run drop > 5% absolute on a primary metric (e.g., EM, F1, similarity) triggers triage

EVAL HARNESS ONBOARDING (SUMMARY STEPS)
1. Create an evalable model artifact: provide model metadata, model-card, and export artifacts per model-onboarding checklist.
2. Add model to eval-harness registry (yaml entry): owner, model-type (decoder/encoder-decoder), quantization supported, expected max-seq, tokenization notes.
3. Provide canonical prompt sets: reference, factuals, safety, instruction tuning, and adversarial prompts.
4. Run baseline evaluation: full-run on standard playbooks (latency, quality, safety, cost) and record outputs in eval database.
5. Create release candidate with tagged eval snapshot and attach to PR / rollout.

PROMPT SET CATALOG GUIDELINES
- Structure: each prompt set must include: id, description, input template, expected output pattern/examples, reference labels, and difficulty tier.
- Coverage: ensure coverage across domains (faq, knowledge, code, instruction-following, analogy) and failure modes (hallucination, repetition, refusal, verbosity).
- Size: Keep benchmark sets small enough for CI (50-500 examples) and larger offline sets for longitudinal monitoring (2k-20k).
- Metadata: label prompts with taxonomy tags: factuality, instruction-following, safety, brevity, numeric-reasoning.

MODEL ONBOARDING ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Functional: Passes baseline eval with no metric regression beyond allowed guardrails (see Key Metrics).
- Performance: Meets latency and throughput SLOs for intended deployment profile (cpu/gpu, batch sizes).
- Cost: Token-cost delta within acceptable range, or approved by product for higher-cost model with documented benefits.
- Safety: No severity-1 safety failures on safety prompt set; severity-2 must be documented + mitigations.
- Observability: Model exposes tracing hooks, token-level logs, and eval snapshot ID.

QUANTIZATION PROFILE PRINCIPLES AND EXAMPLE PROFILES
- Principle: Prefer quantization profiles that preserve critical quality metrics (factuality, semantic similarity) while reducing memory and improving throughput.
- Test matrix: For each quantization profile run: quality eval, lat/throughput bench, KV cache memory usage, and OOM risk scan.

Example profile table (as text):
- profile-id: fp16-standard | expected-impact: baseline quality, memory: medium, recommended-use: production-high-accuracy
- profile-id: int8-dynamic | expected-impact: <=1.5% quality delta, memory: low, recommended-use: cost-sensitive online endpoints
- profile-id: int4-aggressive | expected-impact: up to 5% quality delta (domain dependent), memory: very low, recommended-use: batch/offline or latency-tolerant routes only

QUANTIZATION RISK MATRIX (GUIDELINES)
- If quality delta > 2% on primary dev metrics -> mark profile as experimental and enable canary traffic only.
- If hallucination rate increases > 1.5x baseline -> disallow in production for knowledge-intensive routes.
- If latency improves but cost increases (e.g., more tokens due to decoding differences) -> require product sign-off.

REGRESSION TRIAGE PLAYBOOK (RUNBOOK)
Trigger: regression alert from eval CI or production monitoring where any primary metric crosses regression alert threshold.
1. Triage and severity:
   - Severity-1: production degradation impacting >1% of traffic or critical clients; page SRE and applied-ml.
   - Severity-2: localized regressions (one model route, limited traffic) — notify owners and start investigation.
2. Gather artifacts:
   - Eval snapshot id, model artifact id, quantization profile, rollout ID
   - Relevant prompt examples that triggered regression (attach model outputs)
   - Telemetry: per-route latency, token-cost, error rates, and model-serving logs (trace ids)
3. Quick rollback path (first 30 minutes):
   - If regression correlates to a model change, rollback to previous model version via rollout dashboard.
   - If regression correlates to quantization change, redeploy previous profile or fall back to fp16.
   - If regression correlates to infra change (kernels, runtime), route traffic to dedicated capacity or secondary region.
4. Root-cause process (30 min-6 hours):
   - Reproduce regression in controlled eval-harness with the same prompt sets and seeds.
   - Run A/B with binary search over config deltas: tokenization differences, decoding params (temp, top_k/top_p), stopping rules, and quantization bits.
   - Inspect decoding traces and attention/kv cache behavior if available.
5. Mitigation and verification:
   - Apply fix (model revert, decoding param adjustment, or quantization tuning).
   - Rerun full eval playbook and ensure metrics return within guardrails.
   - For customer-impacting incidents produce postmortem and notify impacted customers.

CI PATTERNS AND ALERTING
- CI gates: every model PR must run the small CI eval suite (50-200 core prompts): quality checks, safety checks, and latency smoke tests.
- Nightly full-run: run extended benchmarks across dataset catalog and quantization profiles.
- Alerting: threshold-based alerts integrated with PagerDuty (eng-sre) and Slack eval-alerts channel.

EXAMPLE EVAL HARNESS CONFIG (YAML)
---
model_id: redwood/rw-xyz-3b
artifact_id: rw-xyz-3b-v1.2.0
profiles:
  - name: fp16-standard
  - name: int8-dynamic
prompt_sets:
  - id: factuals-v1
  - id: safety-v2
dev_metrics:
  - name: embedding_similarity
    comparator: greater_equal
    threshold: 0.78
  - name: hallucination_rate
    comparator: less_equal
    threshold: 0.03
  - name: latency_99p_ms
    comparator: less_equal
    threshold: 200
---
(Place the above under eval-harness registry entry for model onboarding)

TEMPLATES AND CHECKLISTS
- Quick onboarding checklist (short):
  1. Model-card + license review
  2. Tokenizer validation (sample coverage test)
  3. Eval-harness registry entry + prompt sets attached
  4. Baseline eval run + add to dashboard
  5. Observability hooks and tracing enabled
  6. Canary rollout config prepared

- Regression postmortem template fields (to include in incident):
  - Summary, impact, timeline, root cause, mitigations, retrospective actions, owner, date.

RELATED PAGES
See also: eval-harness standards, prompt-set catalog, model-onboarding playbook, quantization-profiles best practices.

APPENDIX: COMMON INVESTIGATION COMMANDS
- Run eval-harness locally: ./tools/eval-harness run --model artifact-id --prompts factuals-v1 --profile int8-dynamic --out /tmp/eval.json
- Compare embedding similarity: python tools/compare_embeddings.py --baseline /tmp/baseline.json --candidate /tmp/eval.json --metric cosine
- Generate prompt sample: python tools/format_prompt_set.py --id safety-v2 --sample 30
